1) a saliency map derived from eye-tracking data can be used to reduce rendering overhead in 2D/ 3D image matching by only processing selective regions of interest, and 2) the saliency maps are derived from eye-tracking scan path data by using a feature normalization process that is robust to differences in background image content and observer visual search strategies.
1) the saliency driven registration method provides a more efficient registration process by reducing the number of pixels that need to be processed in the image similarity measure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extraction of visual saliency features from eye tracking data, and their use for 2D/ 3D image alignment.
the development of new methods for 2D/2D and 2D/ 3D registration using salient image features derived from eye-tracking data.
the development and evaluation of an eye-tracking based technique for deriving saliency maps from a group of observers.

saliency information derived from human visual attention can be used to reduce computational complexity of image registration tasks.
